title: Andy Peretti bitten by Frank Buck's monkey at the World's Fair
summary: At the Flushing Meadows World's Fair, Frank Buck's ape bit Dorsey trumpeter Andy Peretti, who lisped his complaint, and the band broke up laughing.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Another incident you might enjoy, Milt Hinton, I don't know whether you can use it in our biography -- however, while we were at the Pennsylvania Roof, that summer of 1939, we doubled for a couple of weeks at the World's Fair, that was the beginning, the 1939-1940 World's Fair in Flushing Meadows, and we doubled afternoons. They had a band show there, and the people would roam around and then come up to hear the bands of the era, and we were there for two weeks.

And while we were there, a set up of that band shell was across from the Frank Buck display; he was there, he was alive then, with some animals. And we had in the band a wonderful trumpet player, whom I know you worked with, just

a great lead trumpet player. He was with Tommy's band, his name was Andy Peretti, he was well known for his griping, he was an artist at griping, and he was also very beloved by all musicians as a great artist, and they sent Frank Buck over at one of our short intermissions; we were still sitting on the Bandstand, and he came over to get the crowds around and they used to advertise; they'd take times like this to advertise because they had a big crowd listening to our band. So Frank Buck came, however, with a pith helmet and all his array, the jungle suit, the whole works -- with an ape, or a monkey, as you will.
And, he set the monkey on a chair and started to do his spiel about come on over and I'll explain and I'll show you some of our animals and explain some of my expeditions into Africa.

Well, Andy Peretti, who didn't like the looks of the ape -- the ape turned around and stared at him. So Andy stuck out his tongue at him, and the ape didn't like that a bit, and he bit him. Not enough to draw too much blood, but he did bite him. Which broke the band up -- we thought it was very funny. And I don't know -- one of the great things about Andy is that he lisped badly, and he said, 'That thon of a bitch bit me!' Well, that was a laugh in itself, but I don't know whether it was coincidence or what when Frank Buck led the ape off the stand, the ape got sick, which broke the
band up, and of course, we had to take a long intermission to get over that.
